key_insight: Cu feedstock morphology governs impact deformation in cold-sprayed Cu–Al₂O₃ composites: spherical particles localize strain at splat interfaces, while spongy particles distribute strain through ligament collapse.
engineering_relevance: Feedstock morphology offers a design lever alongside spray parameters for tailoring ceramic encapsulation, microstructure, and mechanical performance.
method: Compare deposits made with spherical and spongy Cu feedstocks.
Evaluate mechanical and tribological behavior using micro-compression and wear analyses.
evidence_signal: Multiscale characterization links spherical Cu to refined splat boundaries and larger core grains, and spongy Cu to distributed strain hardening and enhanced ceramic encapsulation, with performance differences reported at comparable reinforcement fractions.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative performance gains or processing window, limiting immediate feedstock-selection guidance.
paper_title: Feedstock morphology governs impact-induced deformation in cold sprayed metal-ceramic composites
